quest.title: Should We Meet Again
quest.description: The Fontinalia Film Festival is coming up. Why not head back to Fontaine? You might just run into some old friends there.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

talks.objective: Find a way to get underwater

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Hey, Chiori. Oh, look who's back! Happy Fontinalia Festival, you two!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Ah, looks like we have a superstar in our midst. How about an autograph, big shot?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Haha, very funny.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: All settled, then?

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yep, the Duke gave his blessing, and I cleared it with the Iudex. During the festival, inmates with good behavior will get a chance to spend some time on the outside.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Under the stringent supervision of the Special Patrol, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wriothesley, it's been a while! Happy Fontinalia Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Does that mean Veronique and her brother will be at the festival?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: During a specific window of time, sure. Doesn't hurt to give the inmates something to look forward to. A little sun'll do them some good, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: This is a friend from your travels, I'm guessing? Thought I heard something along those lines...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, we should make some introductions, huh! Chevreuse, Wriothesley, this is Columbina, a friend we met in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Welcome to Fontaine, Miss Columbina. I bet the weather's been quite an adjustment...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hya...!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Um... And not the good kind, I take it?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: No, I quite like it. It's a lot warmer than Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: ...Then, what was the punch for?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Oh, should I not have done that? The flowers that bloom here are so vibrant, and the people are so kind. I just wanted to become friends as fast as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Ah, so that was meant as a gesture of... friendship. Is that right, Miss Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Mhm... Isn't that what friends do?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Right... Might've been a bit premature in this instance, though...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Your friend here is quite the character...

choices.text: She, uh... doesn't get out much.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good thing we said something. You weren't seriously gonna go around punching every single person in Fontaine, were you?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: No, just the ones I wanted to be friends with.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's not... What Paimon's trying to say is, maybe keep the punches to a minimum until AFTER you're friends with someone...

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: If you say so.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Haha... You're quite the character, Miss Columbina.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: So, are we friends?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: #Of course. Any friend of {NICKNAME} is a friend of mine.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Hya...!

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Oof...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: When it comes to friends, you sure know how to pick 'em.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pfft...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: So Miss Columbina is the lead actress I've been hearing so much about. The whole thing about her... aura is starting to make more sense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You gonna be part of the film this time too, Chevreuse?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: That was the plan. But now that Mr. Xavier has changed the direction, I don't think I'm in quite as many scenes.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: It's all for the best, though. A different crew asked me to help consult on some of their musket work.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Oho, sounds like our trusty musketeer is as popular as ever.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I'm just going where I'm needed. I'm more than willing to help with whatever this production needs as well.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ah, well, speaking of... Would you happen to know if there are scenic locations around the Court of Fontaine that other crews haven't booked?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Hm... The festival's pretty popular this year, so there's not a lot left. You might just have to talk it over with the other productions, and see if they'll let you squeeze in here and there.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I see...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Having trouble finding a filming location?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Yes, we made a last-minute decision to go down a different route, so the indoor locations we reserved are no longer a good fit. And it looks like all of the best outdoor spots have been taken.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Y'know, I might know a place. Good views, good atmosphere... and no production team has snatched it up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds perfect! Where is it?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: You want me to reveal it just like that? C'mon, let it be a surprise.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: As much as that sounds... riveting, I think we should divide and conquer.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You go do that, and Director Furina and I will take Miss Columbina around the city to discuss lighting and styling. Is that alright with you, Miss Columbina?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: #{NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, everyone here is our friend. So, don't worry about a thing and just focus on enjoying your trip!

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Hehe, okay.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: #Alright, then {NICKNAME} and I will go check out this potential filming location. It might even give me some inspiration for the new script!

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I'll leave this to the Duke then. Until later, everyone. Maybe we'll run into each other on set!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, okay then. Lead the way, Wriothesley! Paimon's not built for suspense. Let's get this show on the road!

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Who said anything about "roads"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Huh?

choices.text: She doesn't have much experience with people.

talks.objective: Go to Fontaine and take part in their film festival
Go to Fontaine and take part in their film festival

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No way! You brought the Wingalet up to the surface!?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: It'd make quite the grand backdrop for a film, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's more focused on the fact that this thing is supposed to be underwater... inside the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: True, and keeping up with the maintenance on a vessel this big is a lot of work. It takes a crazy amount of manpower just to keep it up and running.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Paimon kinda thought it just sat there until you needed it...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I wish it were that simple. The truth is, the maintenance costs on this thing are substantial, so we decided to rent it out during the festival to earn some extra mora.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Besides, the inmates are the ones who keep it in good shape. Seeing the fruits of their labor put to use is a good form of social rehabilitation for them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, you've really thought this through.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatcha think, Xavier? Is this a good place to shoot?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ah, I've got it! Good messieurs and mesdemoiselles, I've got it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Gonna take that as a "yes."

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: The beginning is the hardest part, and the opening of this film has been eluding me, but now... I know just how it should start!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Glad to hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks for bringing us here, Wriothesley.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Don't thank me just yet. This isn't quite a done deal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh? Not a done deal as in... someone already rented it out? You said no other production teams had snatched it up!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: This person isn't affiliated with a production team. The rental fee was high enough to scare off plenty of other film crews, but she didn't blink. Made quite the generous offer, and didn't even attempt to haggle.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Do you know what she plans to use it for? I'd like to at least have a rough idea before going in to negotiate.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I didn't ask for the details. But I did see what looked like a "Fishing Permit" and a "Business License" on her desk.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: My guess is she's planning on using it for some kind of restaurant or aquarium.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A floating restaurant is sure to attract people! But an aquarium sounds cool too! The views from the ship make it a great spot for a date!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: The Wingalet might not be under my command right now, but it's always nice to see her admired.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: A film is sure to drum up some good publicity as well. I do hope we can work something out with the current captain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, guess we should head over and talk things out, then.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Best of luck.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, the Wingalet seems even bigger up close... The rooms are so spacious.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wonder who rented it out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello? Anyone there?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Guess not...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Perhaps the captain had business to attend to elsewhere?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, why rent such a massive boat just to have it sit here, without even leaving so much as a note...? Ahem, let's try again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyone there!? Hellooooo!
...Seriously? Right now?
...What is it gonna take to get some decent sleep around here... Is a nap too much to ask for...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *yawn*... Sorry, the aquarium's closed for the— Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C—Citlali!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Paimon! H—Hold on!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This is just great! How am I gonna go out dressed like this!? What happened to my regular clothes!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The wash! I put them in the wash after I drank too much and fell into the fountain... This can't be happening. Am I seriously gonna go out like this!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Think we might've caught her at a bad time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali...?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...I don't wanna hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Hear what?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: A single word about what I'm wearing! No comments. None! Is that clear?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, um... Yep. Crystal.

choices.text: (What's wrong with it? It looks good...)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Huh? Y—You think so?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: No, wait! I told you not to say anything!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I didn't!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Wha... Then what was—

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #({M#His}{F#Her} thoughts... I heard {M#his}{F#her} thoughts. Ah! How could I forget about that!)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: (This is so embarrassing! I seemed a little too pleased to get that compliment, didn't I...)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #(Wait! The mind-reading went both ways... Does that mean {NICKNAME}'s hearing all this too...?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I didn't hear a thing...)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You clearly did!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... What did we do? Paimon's not following...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...Nothing! It's nothing! Let's just move on. Ahem... Did you need something?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You're not here alone, I see...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Ahaha... Hello. I'm Xavier, a film director and producer from Fontaine. I meant to introduce myself sooner. I just didn't want to, um... interrupt, hehehe.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ah, no wonder we ran into each other in Fontaine of all places. You must also be in town for the festival then...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We're helping Xavier with his film. In fact, we were hoping to shoot some scenes on this boat...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're the one who rented it out, right, Citlali?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Me? Rent a boat? I wish I had that kinda spare cash floating around, not to mention the spare time...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Don't get the wrong idea, though! I'm not here to sail off into the sunset and live out some cushy, retirement life, okay? I'm not that old!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then why are you dressed like... Um, how did you end up staying aboard the Wingalet?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Well, I heard one of my favorite light novels was getting turned into a film, so I came to Fontaine to catch the premiere.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Originally, I booked a room near the Opera Epiclese, but I'm quite particular about where I sleep these days. I think it's an age thing, and that bed... I just couldn't sleep in it.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I tried to find a different hotel, but with the festival, everything was completely booked!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Just as I was worried I'd have to sleep under a bridge or something, I happened to spot a "Help Wanted" sign on the side of the road...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So, you're here to take care of the boat?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: No, I was hired to man the front desk. The pay is a bit low, but food and drinks are covered, and it includes room and board during the festival. Plus, the job is simple, so I thought I'd give it a shot.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, they actually thought you'd be a good fit, huh...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: What, you don't think I'm cut out for it?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: All I have to do is tell people the aquarium isn't open yet. Other than that, I'm free to do whatever I want. It's a pretty sweet gig.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's all?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Yeah, I was also kind of shocked, but it's not a lie. Head downstairs and see for yourselves. There's nothing but empty tanks. Not a marine animal in sight.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Did your boss mention anything about being open to film crews using this space? Our production was hoping to film on the deck for a few scenes.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Uh, no... That never came up... You could just ask her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, she's around? What kind of person is she? We should know what we're heading into...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: She's... nice enough, I suppose. Pretty reasonable, too. Even offered for me to move to a bigger cabin if I was too cramped.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Back at the Masters of the Night-Wind, I'm used to being the one giving orders. But working under her doesn't feel like being bossed around. She seems to respect what I think.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, she sounds like a great boss!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: She did tell me she'd rather not be disturbed, though. She's been working on an important project, so I'd keep it brief.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Got it! Thanks for the heads-up!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Alright, the captain's quarters are this way. I can take—

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Wait, but I'm wearing... Ugh, whatever, I doubt she'll care. Just follow me.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Miss Guillotin, these visitors were hoping to ask you about something.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Guillotin...?)
I thought I said to limit the interruptions...
Just tell them the aquarium is still—

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Sandrone? You... You're here!?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Huh? You... know each other?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you okay, Sandrone? Do you still remember us? Everyone was so upset after... what happened. We... We all missed you so much!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Miss Citlali, why don't you escort this gentleman to the reception area for a cup of tea? I have something to discuss with these two in private.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ah... I see. Right this way, Mr. Xavier.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sandrone...?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hah... I really can't go anywhere without running into you two, can I...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you okay? During the battle, your core... It was...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: ...Destroyed by that bastard Dottore? That's right. But as you can see, I'm fine now. No major issues. Or at least, there shouldn't be...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a relief! Why didn't you tell us sooner, or come back to see your friends?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Now that I have the chance, I just want to say...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hm?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you for saving me.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Huh? Ugh... Don't get the wrong idea, I only saved you so we could complete that formula and defeat Dottore once and for all... Even if he did crawl back from the grave to make us all miserable again...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That doesn't matter. You're still a hero.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Alright, alright, but it wasn't just me. All I did was lend my brilliant mind to the cause and take care of one part of the plan. Although, I'm not denying it would have fallen apart without me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, you got that right! You're amazing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But how did you go from a, um... Y'know...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: From a lifeless pile of scrap to looking like this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon was trying to put it a bit more gently, but yeah...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Heh... Where do I even start...

choices.text: (What's wrong with it? It looks cute...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: *cough*... Argh...!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: *panting*... Curse it all...!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Where... am I!?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Did we do it? How much time has passed? I'm not in one of that lunatic's experimental labs, am I?)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Wait, Fontainian decor... books from the Research Institute... Phew... One thing at a time...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Initiate self-diagnostics...!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Assess the extent of the damage, cut power to compromised, non-essential components, then reconstruct available action modules.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Tch, severe damage to the core... Dottore, you bastard...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...! Pulonia...?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Pulonia! Wake up! Activate!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You're in even worse shape than me...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Internal gears and energy circuits are barely intact... Extreme damage to the core, just like me... Rebooting is off the table...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Even if I could repair the damage, I don't know if... *sigh*...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...You used up all your critical energy in those final moments, didn't you? To protect the core of that guy in the hat and the numerological array.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait, the array...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Yes! The prototype is still here.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (But, can I even run it in this state...?)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Whatever... I have to try. I just need to confirm one thing...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Activate the numerological array. Connect the computing core to "my" body.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (*cough*... Just like I thought. It needs too much computing power.)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Cut off power supply to all functions except the thinking module.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Please. I just need to ask one question...)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Initiate query regarding the "Three Moon Sisters." How many living Moon Goddesses are there in possession of the Trilunar Authority?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...One.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Hahaha, it worked. You did it, Columbina. You made it back.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (But... how did "I" survive?)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (The self-diagnostics showed damage severe enough to shut me down for good... What triggered the reboot?)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Huh? A built-in message? Only visible after a core reboot?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: "The Final Gift"...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...! Alain... Were you the one who gave me this second chance...?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (But why now? What activated it?)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hm? What is that...?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: A Vision? Wait, no. I—It's... a "Stellar Linchpin"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A "Stellar Linchpin"? What's that?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You can think of it as a rare kind of Vision. As for what causes one to manifest, well... That's still unknown.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But in Snezhnaya — or in the Fatui's research at least — it's believed to have some connection to the Third Descender.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The Third Descender"? We knew his remains were used to create the Gnoses, but this is the first we're hearing about a Stellar Linchpin.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You knew about the remains? Right, of course. Look who I'm talking to.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yes, the Heavenly Principles used the remains of the Third Descender to create the seven Gnoses as a means to consolidate the archon system.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Visions result from that same system, so extrapolating from there... It's clear that the manifestation of a Vision is also, to some extent, related to the Third Descender. Still following?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sort of...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: For those that wield them, Visions serve as a means to channel elemental power. The same is true of Stellar Linchpins.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The difference is that, when wielding elemental energy, Stellar Linchpin-users often exhibit a unique kind of power that seems to come from beyond Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's believed that, when a Stellar Linchpin manifests, impurities from the remains of the Third Descender get fixed in place. Hence, the name. That's also believed to be the source of the strange power I just mentioned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've heard that Visions can appear when someone has a really strong wish or desire. Stellar Linchpins sound kinda similar, so does that mean...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, don't look at me like that. I've never had any grand wishes or aspirations. Just a list of things that drive me up the wall... So, if you're asking why this thing appeared, I have no clue...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: All I know is that, without it, the "Gift" Alain left me — this built-in second chance — never would have triggered. The damage to my core was too severe...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But thanks to the Stellar Linchpin's manifestation, it did trigger, and after my core rebooted, I was able to repair the damage to my body. I also managed to import the numerological array, along with some of Pulonia's surviving algorithms into this form.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, does that mean Pulonia is...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Yes. Unfortunately, Pulonia is... beyond repair.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we're... so sorry to hear that... But, you also mentioned something about a "Final Gift"...?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yes. Alain often spoke to me about wishes and desires when he was alive.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I suppose he thought there might come a day when I wished for something, and was willing to sacrifice my own life to fulfill it, so he left me a chance to start over.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: No, never.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Alain once said I was his proudest masterpiece. That might sound boastful coming from me, but it's also an undeniable fact.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: After Alain died, I started studying how Pulonia and I worked. Pulonia is essentially a computational machine, so it wasn't difficult to figure out the mechanical principles there.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But, when it came to my own structure, that's when Alain, the Lord-Artificer's true greatness struck me once again.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I attempted to imitate it when I created Katheryne, but in the end, she turned out to be nothing more than a superficial replica.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? B—But... As creations go, Katheryne is super impressive! We were shocked when we first found out she was a puppet!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: No, she's nothing compared to what Alain was able to create. Some of the mechanical principles of my own core are still a complete mystery to me.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Keeping that "Gift" hidden wasn't even a challenge for him.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Just a shame I had to waste it on fighting Dottore. I just couldn't stand the thought of him coming out on top.

choices.text: You gave the world a second chance.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hah, if you put it that way, the world owes me a whole lot then, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but all this still doesn't explain what you're doing here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wriothesley said you rented this ship, and even had some kind of... fishing permit?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Ah, that's because I'm trying to go back to the place Alain and I lived when he was alive. My former home, I suppose you could say.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: The second chance wasn't the only part of the "Gift." According to the message, Alain left me a few other things that are stored in the house we shared together.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I'm hoping that whatever he left me can help fix certain "anomalies" in my rebooted core... and help me understand why I received a Stellar Linchpin in the first place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so go back then. What does that have to do with fishing?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Heh, and to think I'm talking to the saviors of Fontaine. Did you forget that the water levels have been rising for centuries? I can't just go back to the place I used to live, because now, it's underwater.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Right...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: With the rising water levels and changes in terrain... It's not just a matter of finding where it is, but also clearing away any sediment or debris.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: But Fontaine law prohibits unauthorized individuals and organizations from excavating underwater ruins. A Melusine caught me the minute I even made an attempt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why not apply for authorization, then?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: And face the endless slog of Fontainian bureaucracy? No thanks.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Besides, I'm a Fatui Harbinger. The diplomatic implications alone would be enough to give the Gestionnaires at the Palais Mermonia a headache.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: A fishing permit, on the other hand, isn't difficult to obtain at all. Minimal paperwork required, and under the name "Guillotin," the application was a cinch.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, you're... exploiting a legal loophole?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Am I? That underwater home belongs to me. If I happen to chance upon it while doing some "fishing," what's the issue with that?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Of course, I do have to catch some fish to put in the aquarium, just in case the Gestionnaires come to check up on things. That's also the reason I hired someone to man the front desk.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... But, isn't that kind of a waste? You went to all the trouble of getting a business license, and rented out this giant ship... just for show?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: If you want to run an aquarium that bad, be my guest. Use the facilities however you want. I'm certainly not going to stop you.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: All I want is to go back home and see what other gifts Alain wanted me to inherit.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Hold on, enough about me... What are you two even doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (Ugh! Seriously! They've been in there forever!)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (The reaction when they saw each other was... strange to say the least. They're lucky I was nice enough to leave the room and give them some space! Back in the Masters of the Night-Wind, I'm the one who gets to kick people out!)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (I just wanna know what they're talking about... Should I cast a little eavesdropping spell?)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (No, what am I thinking? I'm Granny Itztli, the Great Shaman of the Masters of the Night-Wind. I can't do something like that!)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: (This is just ridiculous! Making me wait out here for so long... Where's their respect for their elders!?)

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ah, here they are.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Were you back there arguing or something? What took you so long?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: The two of you are already acquainted with Miss Guillotin, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh, yep! But, don't worry. We got everything sorted! Sandrone agreed to let us shoot on the ship, but it has to be when she's not here.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: When she's not here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, haha...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: You'll excuse me if I didn't exactly ask for this little reunion. I wasn't planning on seeing anyone.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Like I said, my core is severely damaged. Even with the "Gift," there are "anomalies" that are making things unstable.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I don't even know if I can continue to function without issues, so the priority is to fix these "anomalies" and get answers to my own questions. Then, I can see the people that need seeing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, just let Sandrone know when you plan to film, Xavier, and she'll, uh... steer clear.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: I do hope I'm not causing Miss Guillotin too much trouble.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no. She just wants to keep a low profile for her own, uh... complicated reasons. She doesn't want anyone else to know she's here.

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Understood. I'll be sure to keep that in mind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and Citlali...?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She wants to talk to you.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You mean... Miss Guillotin?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: What does she want...? Please don't let it be about the pajamas...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: What!? The Seventh of the Fatui Harbingers?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Why are you telling me all this?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: #I asked {NICKNAME} about you, and I've decided it's best to be open in this instance.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I can understand if you would rather not work for a Harbinger.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: #Regardless, the room on the ship is yours to keep. You're an acquaintance of {NICKNAME}, and I plan to honor that.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: (Wait, she's actually... nice?)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: It's not a problem. The Captain also worked for the Fatui, and he helped Natlan a great deal. We know that there are good people among your ranks.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Besides, I've been around long enough to know what it means to earn one's keep. This isn't Natlan, and I don't expect special treatment. Besides, sitting at a desk isn't exactly backbreaking work.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: I appreciate that perspective, Great Shaman.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Citlali. Just call me Citlali. That title makes me sound so old...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: #Well, Citlali, {NICKNAME} and I are looking for something, so we'll be heading underwater together soon. I'll leave the ship in your care while we're gone.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: T—Together? How... How often?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Not too often. We're heading out in a bit, but I'll be available if you need something.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You couldn't, um... go alone?

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: #I wanted to, but {M#he}{F#she} was concerned about my... physical well-being. So {M#he}{F#she} offered to come with.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Ugh, guess my mental well-being means nothing, then!

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright, our first stop is the Beryl Region. After Alain left the Fontaine Research Institute, he lived in seclusion somewhere around there.

choices.text: I have a few other things to do first...

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Fine. I'll wait here. We can head out once you're done.

talks.objective: Explore the underwater area in the Beryl Region

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Poisson isn't too far from here, right? It's all a bit nostalgic, I guess. Back when I lived here, all this was still above water.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alright, I have a general understanding of the terrain changes and sediment accumulation. We can stop here for now.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That went smoother than expected. I appreciate the help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No problem! You doing okay, though, Sandrone? Seeing your home look nothing like you remember... That can't be easy.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'm fine. Times change, people change. That's the one thing you can actually count on. I made peace with that a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You should head back and put them into the aquarium tanks. We finished ahead of schedule, so your crew is probably still on the ship. I'll follow in a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, Xavier said he was gonna test out a couple of shots.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure you don't want us to come with?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'm sure. I want to take another look around on my own.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, then! Want us to let you know when the filming is done?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: No need. Columbina relies on kuuvahki to perceive her surroundings. In Nod-Krai, her senses are heightened because kuuvahki is everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But, here, as long as she doesn't activate her abilities, her range of perception should be equivalent to an average person's line of sight. I figured that out back in Snezhnaya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's... oddly specific.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I have hiding from her down to a science. So, what? Things might be a bit different now that she's merged with the Moon Sisters, but I doubt there's been a drastic change.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: The point is, you two can head back. Don't worry about me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, if you say so. Come find us on the ship if you need anything!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What did you leave for me, Alain? Did you know I would come back? Or... did you make it so I would have to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xavier! We're back!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Shh! Quiet on set! They're filming over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oops! Sorry!
What's your take, Detective?

dialogues.speaker: "Detective"
dialogues.text: Hmm... Bullet-wound to the chest, gunpowder residue on the clothes... The victim must have been shot at close range.
You think it was someone they knew?

dialogues.speaker: "Detective"
dialogues.text: Yes. It's possible the suspect arranged for them to meet at this very spot.

dialogues.speaker: "Hurlock"
dialogues.text: Hmm, a reasonable deduction. But... You're overlooking a crucial clue!

dialogues.speaker: "Detective"
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: "Hurlock"
dialogues.text: ...The victim's pocket watch is missing.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: And... cut!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: I think we got it! Good work, everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Phew... Finally!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Acting was nerve-wracking for me when I first tried it too. Just loosen up, and you'll get used to it in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chevreuse! Charlotte!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh! Hello there, you two!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're filming here too? Oh, so Charlotte's crew must've been the one that asked you to help out, huh, Chevreuse!

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Yup, they heard about a potential filming location and wanted to come check it out.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: But, when we got here, your crew had already beaten us to it! Hehe, luckily, Xavier and our director, Lepine-Pauline, go way back. In the end, we agreed to just share each other's filming locations.

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: Considering all the last-minute changes, that's just what Musketeer Pictures needed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: For sure. Based off the scene just now, you must be the star of the film, Charlotte!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hehe, you bet! This detective costume really suits me, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Oh, for sure. You're already right at home lurking in the shadows taking pictures of this and that. Add a notepad, and you're practically method.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Thanks, Miss Chiori! I appreciate the compliment!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That didn't sound much like a compliment to Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: So this is a film set? It looks like a very happy place.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: This must all be quite new to you, Miss Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Yes. I watched a few films with a friend once, but she thought there was no point if I wouldn't open my eyes, so she stopped inviting me.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Looks like I missed out on a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, now you get to make up for it.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: True. But being an actor seems like a tough job...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh? Most people would swap lives with an actor in a heartbeat. The lifestyle is so glamorous, and the pay is more than generous...

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: But they have to act out lives that aren't their own, with the whole world watching on in judgment. If they don't do it justice, it must feel like... they're letting people down.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (That's... exactly how it feels! This young lady has quite the unique perspective...)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Well, that's true. But, these actors are here because they want to be, and they think it's fun. Ahem, most of them at least...

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Not to mention, the film we're shooting is based entirely on you, Miss Columbina. You just need to be true to yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I don't have to pretend to be someone I'm not?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Not at all! Authenticity is what we're after. For example, this first scene opens with you on the boat, sailing to your friend's homeland.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You just need to think about that moment in the story, and picture how you would feel.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Oh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: We're all here? Wonderful. Let's head to the deck and get shooting.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh, and this is for you, dear Paimon. Your clapperboard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Is this the same one Paimon used for "The Two Musketeers"?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: The very same. I saved it just for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Xavier! Feels like being reunited with an old friend!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you keep my Kamera too?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: #Haha, of course. That said, I have a different job in mind for you this time, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Our film is focusing on a single protagonist, so conveying the subtle changes in her state of mind is of the utmost importance.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: In addition to the actor's own performance, another way we can convey that is through "lighting."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But there's already a lighting specialist, isn't there?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: #Yes, but it's clear {NICKNAME} and Miss Columbina share a deep bond. You might have a better chance of understanding her frame of mind in certain scenes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: So, what do you say? Willing to take on the role of "lighting specialist"?

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: It's settled! I leave the job of translating our leading lady's inner thoughts in your capable hands!

choices.text: Not sure I want to give up the coveted title of "Kamera operator," though...

response.speaker: Xavier
response.text: Then, we'll combine them! You can be the "chief lighting and Kamera specialist," haha!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Alright, without any further ado, it's time for production on our film, "A Homecoming," to officially begin!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Turning it over to you once again, Director Furina.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright! Positions, everyone. Kamera Operator, Clapper Loader, get set up! Let me know when lighting is good to go!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: All you need to worry about, Miss Columbina, is hitting your mark. Other than that, just focus on immersing yourself in the emotions of the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Good. Lighting, are we ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ready!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright, quiet on set! Three, two, one, action!

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: This is... her homeland...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Columbina...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: And... cut!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hm, the emotions I'm looking for were definitely there. Let's just try to keep it a bit more natural.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, but definitely keep that gesture at the end. I loved how real it felt — you looked genuinely moved. Alright, if you're ready, let's go for another take.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Uh, Miss Columbina...?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (That presence... It kind of felt like...)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: ...Sandrone?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Hah, see? Told you they'd be here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Xavier! Oh, and Chiori and Furina too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Happy Fontinalia Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ah! Hydro Archon above! If it isn't my darling Kamera operator and clapper loader! A very happy Fontinalia Festival to you as well!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'm guessing you came back to celebrate with us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! And help out, too. Even though the last festival had some... unexpected hiccups, making the film was still super fun!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since you're all here together like this, you must be planning on entering the competition, right?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Of course! A celebration of the entertainment industry? Hehe, no one who's anyone would choose to sit this one out. It only happens once a year, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Fontaine Fashion Week might be more my speed, but the Film Festival brings in a lot of orders and boosts brand recognition. So, I wasn't going to miss out either.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: A few new awards have been added this year, too! "Best Director," "Best Costume Design"... Oh, and "Best Kamera Operation."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Sounds like we've got work to do! C'mon, tell us! What's Musketeer Pictures' film gonna be about?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh, um... About that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's wrong, Xavier? What's with that look? Oh, man, you weren't scammed by some shady investor again, were you!?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: No, no! Even I'm not naive enough to fall for something like that again.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Besides, thanks to the fine people here, Musketeer Pictures has more than enough funds to shoot without investors.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: And yet problems persist...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Ahaha... Well, we were planning to replicate our past success and shoot a film based on a popular novel.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: But, as we were holding auditions for the female lead earlier today, a striking young mademoiselle wandered in by accident.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Her disposition was simply ethereal, the look in her eyes somewhat melancholic... Oh, I wish you could have been there! The awe I felt can scarcely be put to words!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, sounds like she made quite the impression...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: You had to be there, friend. No matter where she stood, it was as if her surroundings, even the air itself, turned into the perfect shot!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess you found your lead actress, then...

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: No, quite the opposite. My script is entirely unworthy of her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sure it's not that bad.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: I fear it is. Nevertheless, I couldn't help but approach the mademoiselle to ask about her background, and what brought her to Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What did she say?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Sadly, she said her best friend was gone. After returning to her own homeland not too long ago, she decided to visit where her friend was from, to remember them better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder she looked sad.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Yes, but that's when it struck me — why not cast her as the lead in a film centered around her search for this old friend?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? You're gonna rewrite the whole script? But, is there even enough time? Isn't the prep work super complicated? We might not finish!

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Think about the difficulties we faced with "The Two Musketeers." We had to start from scratch back then, too. I'd say we're ahead of the game this time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess so, but...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Paimon. Chiori and I have evaluated the proposal, and we support Xavier's decision.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I won't really need to start on the costumes until the cast is finalized, so it's not too much extra work for me.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Oh, fair mademoiselles, how can I ever thank you?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori & Furina
dialogues.text: Finishing the script would be a start.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Y'know, compared to a commercial popcorn flick, I do prefer the idea of shooting a more artistic film — one that leaves a profound and lingering impact in the hearts of the audience!

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm, I agree. True trendsetters are the people who dare to go against the grain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, leave it to Director Furina to have a vision! Honestly though, the artistic passion of everyone at Musketeer Pictures is inspiring!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, now that we've heard so much about this lead actress, Paimon's gotta know who it is!
...Hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waah...! Columbina!? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Hello. I was just walking past when I heard you talking about me, so I came over.

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Huh? You know Miss Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! Wait a second, does this mean... Columbina is the actress who inspired the whole rewrite!?

choices.text: Xavier's reaction seems a lot more reasonable now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait so, did you make the trip by yourself, Columbina?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Yes. I mentioned how I wanted to visit other nations once things settled down in Nod-Krai, remember?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: So I went to the Curatorium to ask Nefer for advice. She told me about the film festival in Fontaine and said it might be fun to visit.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: I spoke to Lauma before I left too, and she thought it was a great idea to get out for a bit. It's just... I received quite different travel advice from the two of them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, how so?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Well, Lauma told me to go out and experience new things and make new friends.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What a wonderful suggestion! That's how a trip should be!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What about Nefer?

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: She said... "Don't trust anyone" and "don't talk to strangers."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep... That sounds like her...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I can understand that too. It shows this Nefer cares about you a great deal, Miss Columbina.

response.speaker: Columbina
response.text: Yes. So I plan on combining their advice. All I need to do is turn strangers into friends, and then I can talk to them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that kinda makes sense, but also... not...

choices.text: Quite a few things are starting to make sense...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh, I wanna ask for an autograph so bad, but I can't do it dressed like this!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: An autograph? From who?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The cast of "Great Detective Hurlock," duh! I came all the way here just for the premiere!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But I didn't expect to end up on their film set! Ah, my laundry just won't dry! The weather here is too wet!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh, I didn't expect to run into you two on set! Happy Fontinalia Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nice acting back there, Charlotte!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Thanks! I'm, uh... usually the one behind the Kamera, so it's actually pretty nerve-wracking being the center of all that attention.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: But, I've known Miss Lepine-Pauline for quite some time, so we work really well together.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Miss Lepine-Pauline prefers to assign roles based on our own personalities. She'll even adjust the script to make it a better fit.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: The scene from earlier was just me and Chevreuse, but Navia and Emilie are also going to be taking part!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! That's quite the lineup!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Your film's leading lady also seems like quite the score. Just on first impressions alone, it's clear she's someone special!

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hehe, guess we'll just have to wait and see who wins Best Picture and gets to go home with the Furina Award!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Hmm... Seeing all the sets in place, things are looking even better than I expected. The actors are doing great too. Editing it all together's gonna be a piece of cake! Bet I can finish it in one night!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi, Lepine-Pauline!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Hey, you're back! The timing couldn't be more perfect! If there's one thing you absolutely can't miss, it's the Fontinalia Film Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And you're a director this time! That's so cool!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Haha, it's all thanks to my apprentice, Ninette. She's the one who told me to read "Great Detective Hurlock" in the first place, and then it struck me — this would make a great film!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about your savings, though? You didn't...

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Haha! Yep! I went all in!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah... Paimon was worried you'd say that.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Relax, it's different this time. I met Director Xavier back during my Kamera outsourcing days, so I got to know the industry a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: I know exactly what our film needs, and what the fans want to see.

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: So, be sure to check it out! I'm confident we've got a winner on our hands!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like it! But we've got some filming chops ourselves! It's definitely still anyone's game!

dialogues.speaker: Lepine-Pauline
dialogues.text: Then, may the best film win!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Terrific performance, Miss Columbina. Truly excellent work.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: Thank you, Director Furina.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: You really don't mind me not taking off my eye mask?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Not at all. Xavier and I already talked it over.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: The character is based on you, so there's no need to change what you're accustomed to doing. Besides, the mask could become one of the defining traits of our film's leading lady!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Just like you suggested, we'll leave the reveal to the more important moments.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Just... be quick about the whole thing, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Xavier
dialogues.text: Miss Guillotin is so generous. We talked it over, and she agreed to let our crew come over and do some test shots while you two are out.
